content.text: : usually first line for menorrhagia that is cyclical & predictable
: active/previous thromboembolic disease, concurrent use w/ hormonal contraceptives, acquired disturbances of color vision
: only IUD indicated for treatment of menorrhagia in women who use intrauterine contraception
: irregular bleeding/spotting, cramping, breast tenderness, mood changes, acne
: 150 mg IM every 90 days has been used to treat menorrhagia
: irregular breakthrough bleeding, breast tenderness, nausea, weight gain, mood disturbances, reduction in BMD
: inhibits GnRH release, suppresses both LH and FSH midcycle surges, and inhibits ovarian steroidogenic enzymes that cause estrogen production
Net effect is production of a hypoestrogenic environment which induces amenorrhea and endometrial atrophy
: bone pain, loss of bone density, hypoestrogenic effects (hot flashes, night sweats, vaginal dryness)
